column4: A tall gothic cathedral stained-glass window, a true leaded-glass mosaic in the manner of medieval and Harry Clarke windows, showing a serene icon of the girl from the character sheet (long orange hair, maid headdress, flower ornament), arms low and open, palms up, gentle downcast gaze. Everything, including her face, is cut from large flat panes of colored glass: the face is a mosaic of about six big panes (ivory and pale orange) separated by thick black lead cames of the same weight as everywhere else in the window, so the face clearly reads as assembled glass that could break apart. Eyes and mouth are painted simply inside panes. No hairline cracks.

Redraw this stained-glass window as a true leaded-glass mosaic. Keep the composition, pose and colors. The girl's face, neck and hands must be cut into large separate glass panes (like a jigsaw of about six pieces for the face) with thick black lead lines exactly as heavy as the lead lines in her dress and the tracery. The lead lines are bold and smooth, never thin cracks. Eyes and mouth stay whole and serene.

Redraw this as true leaded-glass mosaic windows, keeping composition and poses. Each girl's face is cut into a few large glass panes by bold black lead lines of the same weight as in the dress (one line along the hairline, one beside the nose down to the jaw, one across the cheek); skin panes stay ivory; nothing covers the eyes, nose or mouth; no bands, masks or blindfolds; no thin cracks.
